task.description: TEST-DESIGNER: write test specs and test code for REQ-187's timer-arm/timer-fire/cancellation wiring, per .claude/agents/test-designer.md. Both idiom (REVIEWER) and security (SECURITY-REVIEWER) gates have passed -- this step is mutation-driven coverage against the original acceptance criteria, not a re-litigation of design choices.
acceptance_criteria: AC1/AC7: a token reaching a valid :TIMER node arms exactly one 'pending' timers row with fire_at = arrival + parsed duration_iso8601; cover at least one date-part and one time-part duration string, plus the P0D edge case.

AC2: the timer row and the state-transition event are written in the SAME transaction -- a test that forces the :event step (or equivalent) to fail after the timer-arm Multi.merge step must leave NO timers row behind.

AC3: firing a timer (Scheduler.poll_and_fire/1 or a direct do_fire/fire_timer path) advances the live token off the :TIMER node along its outgoing edge, including the case where that edge leads directly into another dispatch-needing node (:TIMER->:TIMER, :TIMER->:EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, :TIMER->:SUB_PROCESS) resolving fully in one advance_after_timer_fired/3 call.
AC4: completing an instance (the :completed path through finalize_instance_projection/5) cancels its 'pending' timers via cancel_pending_timers/5, called from the same, unmoved call site.

AC5: cancel_instance/3 cancels 'pending' timers in the same transaction as the cancellation event; a test forcing a later Multi step to fail (e.g. :event) must leave any timer seeded for that instance still 'pending' -- verifying run_cancel_instance/5's :timer_cancellations step (positioned between :open_tasks and :instance_projection) rolls back correctly.

AC6 (SCH-03): a 'fired' timer is never mutated by a later cancellation (status-guarded update_all, WHERE status = 'pending'); no 'pending' timer belonging to a terminal instance is ever fired by a later poll. Cover the concurrency-shaped edge case at the unit/integration level available to TEST-DESIGNER (does not need real concurrent Postgres transactions if a deterministic ordering can exercise both branches of the race).

The multi-timer-per-hop-chain guard: a :PARALLEL_GATEWAY split landing two branches on distinct :TIMER nodes in the same hop-chain must surface prepare_timer_arms/4's {:error, {:multiple_timers_in_one_hop_chain_not_supported, node_ids}} as a typed, non-raising failure -- add a regression test for this specific scenario since it is new, defensive logic beyond the design doc's original description (REVIEWER's own item, see req187-reviewer-report.md).
Purity regression: keep transition.ex's own grep-based purity check (see its moduledoc) exercised as part of this requirement's test suite if not already wired into a standing check.
Reconstruction: replaying a persisted TIMER_FIRED event (Reconstruction.replay/4) reproduces the same post-fire InstanceState the live advance_after_timer_fired/3 path produces, independently.
No route/controller/migration/web/ file should need touching to add this coverage (AC8) -- flag to REVIEWER if it turns out one does.
